chunks: From him, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Jamil ibn Darrāj and Muhammad ibn Humrān, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

At whatever hour she sees blood, then it breaks the fasting woman's fast when she menstruates. And if she sees purity at some hour of the day, she makes up the prayer of the day; and the night is likewise.

key_terms.تُفَطِّرُ: causes the fast to be broken or invalidated
key_terms.قَضَتْ: she makes up what is due afterward
key_terms.ٱلدَّمَ: menstrual blood seen by the woman
key_terms.ٱلصَّائِمَةَ: the woman who is observing sawm (fasting)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a fasting woman begins menstruation or becomes pure during the day?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning menstruation in relation to sawm (fasting) and salat (prayer). It states that the onset of menstrual blood invalidates the fast, and that when a woman becomes pure during the day or night, she makes up the corresponding prayer.
